areas.area_name: Mine (open-cut gibbsitic bauxite, India East Coast plateau type: clearing, topsoil and laterite-cap stripping, bench drill & blast, selective load & haul, ROM pad, primary sizing, grade control, dewatering, rehabilitation)
areas.purpose: Deliver on average ~5.9 Mt/yr wet (~5.3 Mt/yr dry) of run-of-mine (ROM) gibbsitic bauxite with controlled quality (available Al2O3, reactive SiO2) to the mine primary sizing station and overland conveyor. Tonnage mined equals refinery consumption plus or minus stock change. Mined land is rehabilitated progressively. DEPOSIT MODEL (fixed in this revision): India East Coast khondalite-plateau lateritic bauxite of the Panchpatmali / Baphlimali / Lanjigarh-supply type. The profile is topsoil 0.1-0.3 m, then a laterite/ferricrete cap 1-5 m, then a compact to hard bauxite horizon 10-30 m thick (design average ~12-18 m), then a lithomarge/kaolinitic clay floor (high reactive silica) over khondalite. Darling Range practice (thin 4-8 m friable ore, free-dig below a blasted caprock, ~60-110 ha/yr disturbance) is kept only as a comparison note.
areas.process_description: 1) Planning and grade control. Exploration drilling on a grid of about 60-120 m (in-fill to ~50 m) defines the ore body. Grade-control drilling uses RC on a ~12.5-25 m grid with 1 m intervals through the full ore column, supplemented by sampling of blast-hole cuttings on every bench. Samples are assayed by XRF and by a laboratory low-temperature caustic micro-digestion (~143-150 degC). This reports AVAILABLE Al2O3 (gibbsite alumina) and REACTIVE SiO2 (kaolinite silica, which forms desilication product in the refinery). Bench-by-bench ore/waste and grade-bin polygons are loaded into excavator GNSS guidance and the fleet management system (FMS). Grid spacings are engineering estimates. 2) Clearing. Dozers remove vegetation and merchantable timber; mulch is kept for rehabilitation. 3) Topsoil stripping. The top ~0.1-0.3 m, which holds the seed bank, is stripped separately and either returned directly to rehabilitation or stockpiled in low piles under 2 m high. 4) Laterite cap removal. The 1-5 m cap is ripped where it is soft or drilled and blasted where it is hard ferricrete. Depending on its available alumina and reactive silica, it is loaded either as waste (to backfill or dumps) or as low-grade ore for blending. Strip ratio is ~0.1-0.4 t waste per t ore (engineering estimate). 5) Ore benching by drill & blast (base case). The 10-30 m bauxite is mined on 5-8 m benches (2-4 benches per pit), with ramps no steeper than 8%. Holes are 115-165 mm DTH, pattern ~3.5 x 4.0 to 4.5 x 5.0 m, with 0.5-1.0 m subdrill. Powder factor is ~0.25-0.45 kg/bcm of bulk emulsion or ANFO, with electronic initiation. About 3.0-3.5 Mbcm/yr of ore plus hard cap is blasted, needing ~200-300 km/yr of drilling (engineering estimates). The lowest bench is stopped above the clay floor as directed by grade control, because the lithomarge is high in reactive silica. ALTERNATIVE: surface miners (Wirtgen 2200SM/2500SM class) cut the ore in 0.3-0.6 m layers without blasting. This is used near villages and forest, or where very selective floor control is needed. 6) Load and haul. 200-t class hydraulic backhoe excavators (and a 992-class wheel loader) load ~90-t rear-dump trucks. Trucks haul 2-6 km on engineered haul roads, either directly to the primary sizer dump hopper or to grade-bin fingers on the ROM pad. The FMS assigns trucks to faces so that the delivered blend meets targets: reactive SiO2 under the agreed ceiling, available Al2O3 over the floor. Mine roster is 2 x 12 h shifts, 7 days/week. Trucks achieve ~5,000-5,500 operating h/yr; production is lost on monsoon heavy-rain days. 7) Primary sizing. Trucks dump into a 2-sided hopper. An apron feeder draws ore into a twin-shaft primary sizer that reduces blasted ROM (top size ~1.0-1.5 m) to -200 mm for the 1,200 mm overland belt. Nominal rate is ~1,100-1,250 t/h over ~5,000-5,500 effective h/yr; the 1,800 t/h design gives surge capacity and allows pre-monsoon stock build. A pedestal rock breaker handles oversize. A self-cleaning magnet and metal detector protect the belts. 8) Dewatering and water management. Pits are rainfall-fed and deepen to 10-30 m, so the sumps collect large monsoon inflows. Diesel dry-prime pumps lift water to sediment ponds. Clean-water diversion drains route runoff around the pits, and haul roads are watered to suppress dust. 9) Rehabilitation. Because ore thickness (10-30 m) far exceeds waste volume, pits cannot be fully backfilled. Waste and cap are placed back on the pit floor, walls are reshaped to stable batters or left as benches, and topsoil is spread. The floor is deep-ripped on the contour and planted or seeded with local species. The final landform is a lowered plateau surface. Clearing to rehabilitation takes ~1-3 years per mining block. NOTES: Darling Range ore (~27-33% available Al2O3, quartz-rich, thin) gives a larger tonnage per t of alumina and is mostly free-dig. High-temperature (boehmitic) deposits such as Weipa or Guinea are mined similarly; the differences lie in the refinery, not the mine. Ore loss and dilution are an in-situ-to-ROM reconciliation only: dilution lowers the delivered grade, which is already reflected in the bauxite factor, and does not add tonnes to the refinery feed.

streams.name: ROM bauxite (ore) to primary sizer / ROM pad
streams.from_to: Pits (01-EX / 01-FL loading 01-HT trucks) -> 01-HP-001 dump hopper or 01-RP-001 ROM pad
streams.flow: ~5.9 Mt/yr wet average (~5.3 Mt/yr dry) = refinery consumption +- stock change; ~1,100-1,250 t/h nominal while crushing (~5,000-5,500 effective h/yr); peak tipping up to ~2,000 t/h
streams.composition: Design ore as delivered (after dilution): total Al2O3 45-48%, available Al2O3 ~40% (range 38-43%), reactive SiO2 1.5-2.5% (blend ceiling ~2.5%), total SiO2 2-5%, Fe2O3 18-25%, TiO2 1.5-3%, LOI ~24-26%; free moisture 8-12% (higher in monsoon). Blasted lump size up to ~1.0-1.5 m
streams.basis: 2.0 Mt/yr alumina x bauxite factor 2.65 = 5.3 Mt dry; /0.90 = 5.9 Mt wet. India East Coast-type grade per published descriptions (Authier-Martin et al. 2001; Hudson et al., Ullmann's). Ore loss/dilution is an in-situ-to-ROM adjustment only (engineering estimate)

streams.name: Overburden, laterite cap waste
streams.from_to: Pits -> backfill of mined-out pit floors / temporary waste dumps
streams.composition: Lateritic soil, low-grade ferricrete/laterite cap, occasional kaolinitic clay
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: strip ratio ~0.1-0.4 t/t for a 1-5 m cap over 10-20 m ore (corrected from 1.5-3.5 Mt/yr)

streams.name: Topsoil
streams.from_to: Cleared areas -> direct return to rehabilitation or topsoil stockpiles
streams.flow: ~20,000-135,000 m3/yr (20-45 ha/yr x 0.1-0.3 m), plus haul-road and dump clearing
streams.composition: Organic-rich surface soil with seed bank; handled when dry to moist, never when saturated

streams.name: Bulk explosives
streams.composition: Ammonium nitrate emulsion / ANFO (wet holes: emulsion only); boosters and electronic detonators from 01-MZ magazine

streams.name: Sized ore to overland system
streams.basis: Engineering estimate consistent with a 1,200 mm belt (CEMA lump-size guidance)

streams.name: Pit dewatering water
streams.from_to: Pit sumps -> 01-PP-001..004 -> 01-SP-001 sediment ponds -> reuse for dust suppression / controlled discharge
streams.flow: Highly seasonal; design ~150-300 L/s per active pit group in monsoon storms
streams.composition: Rainwater with suspended clay/bauxite fines (TSS can exceed 1,000 mg/L before settling)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; size to the site design storm (e.g. 1-in-10 yr 72 h)

streams.name: Haul-road dust-suppression water
streams.from_to: Sediment ponds / raw-water standpipes -> 01-WC water carts -> haul roads
streams.basis: Engineering estimate (approx. 0.5-2 L/m2 per application, several passes per shift)

equipment.name: Grade-control drill rig (RC) with sample splitter
equipment.function: Drills grade-control holes through the full 10-30 m ore column ahead of mining and recovers representative 1 m samples for available Al2O3, reactive SiO2 and Fe2O3 assays. These define ore boundaries, the floor contact and grade bins for each bench.
equipment.type_selected: Track- or truck-mounted reverse-circulation (RC) rig with on-board compressor, cyclone and rotary cone splitter
equipment.why_this_type: Gives dry chip samples with low contamination at 1 m resolution through hard laterite cap and compact bauxite. Aircore is too weak for the hard East Coast ore; RC is needed.
equipment.alternatives: Diamond core (exploration and QAQC only, slow); blast-hole cuttings sampling (cheap, coarse support, used as a supplement); FTIR/DRIFTS on drill powders for rapid screening of available alumina and reactive silica.
key_dimensions: Rig footprint ~10-12 m long x 2.5-3 m wide, mast ~8-10 m high when raised (engineering estimate)
Hole diameter ~115-140 mm; depth typically 15-35 m (through the cap and ore to the clay floor)
Grade-control grid ~12.5-25 m vs exploration 60-120 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: Available Al2O3 and reactive SiO2 (low-temperature micro-digestion ~143-150 degC), XRF total oxides, LOI

equipment.working_principle: Compressed air drives a down-the-hole hammer at the bit. A dual-wall rod string returns the cuttings up the inner tube (reverse circulation), so chips from the bit face are not mixed with wall material. The cuttings pass through a cyclone that drops the solids into a rotary cone splitter. The splitter divides each interval into a laboratory sub-sample of ~2-5 kg and a reject, and sample bags are numbered by hole and depth. In the laboratory the samples are dried, crushed, pulverised and digested in caustic at low temperature to replicate refinery digestion. This gives available alumina and reactive silica, the two numbers that drive refinery economics. The results feed a block model that defines bench ore polygons, the floor contact and grade bins.
details_to_model: Crawler or 6x6 truck carrier with folding mast (lattice or box section), rod carousel holding ~6 m dual-wall rods
Top-drive rotation head running on mast rails; dust hood at the collar
Cyclone (~0.6 m dia) on a frame beside the mast, with flexible sample hose from the rod head
Rotary cone splitter under the cyclone; numbered calico/plastic sample bags on a rack; reject piles laid out in rows on the ground
Auxiliary booster compressor trailer; water tank for dust suppression
Collars marked by survey pegs/flags; grid of drilled holes with sample piles in rows on the bench
Operator cabin or control panel with emergency stop; rod-handler cage guarding the rotating rods
hazards_and_safety: Rotating rods and rod handling (entanglement, pinch points): guarding, interlocked rod handler
High-pressure air hoses: whip checks on all couplings
Respirable dust including crystalline silica: dust hood, water injection, P2 respirators
Working near bench crests: edge bunds, set-back rules
Noise above 100 dB(A): hearing protection
sources: Authier-Martin M., Forte G., Ostap S., See J. (2001) The mineralogy of bauxite for producing smelter-grade alumina, JOM 53(12):36-40
Donoghue A.M., Frisch N., Olney D. (2014) Bauxite mining and alumina refining: process description and occupational health risks, J Occup Environ Med 56(5S):S12-S17
ISO 8685 Aluminium ores - Sampling procedures; ISO 6140 Aluminium ores - Preparation of samples
Engineering estimate for rig dimensions and grid
operating_tips_and_key_points: Reactive silica, not total silica, drives caustic soda and alumina losses (DSP); grade control must report it.
Locate the lithomarge (clay floor) contact precisely; it sets the last bench floor.
Insert field duplicates and certified reference materials (QAQC) at ~1 in 20 samples.
Avoid drilling wet clay during heavy rain because of smearing and sample bias.

equipment.name: Crawler top-hammer / DTH blast-hole drill rigs (caprock)
equipment.function: Drill blast holes in the hard laterite cap and in the compact-to-hard bauxite benches (5-8 m) to fragment them for selective loading.
equipment.type_selected: Self-propelled crawler surface drill rig, down-the-hole (DTH) hammer, 115-165 mm holes, with on-board high-pressure screw compressor, rod changer, dry dust collector and GNSS hole navigation (Epiroc FlexiROC D65 / Sandvik DI650i-DP1500i class)
equipment.why_this_type: About 3.0-3.5 Mbcm/yr of ore and hard cap must be blasted. DTH rigs of 115-165 mm suit 5-8 m benches, give good fragmentation control in the 20-80 MPa material and keep ground vibration low near villages. They tram quickly between pits. Fleet: ~200-300 km/yr drilled at ~12-16 bcm per drilled metre; each rig gives ~70-120 km/yr (~20-30 m/h effective x ~3,500-4,000 drilling h), so 3 operating + 1 standby (engineering estimate).
equipment.alternatives: Surface miners (01-SM, cut instead of blast); ripping with D10/D11 dozers where cap or ore is soft; top-hammer rigs (89-127 mm) for cap-only drilling; large rotary drills (unsuitable for short benches).
key_dimensions: Rig ~11-13 m long (boom stowed), ~2.5-3.0 m wide, feed/mast ~9-12 m (OEM class, approximate)
Mass ~20-28 t (OEM class, approximate)
Hole dia 89-127 mm; depth ~1.5-5 m (caprock 0.5-3 m + 0.3-0.5 m sub-drill); pattern 2.5-3.5 x 3.0-4.0 m, nominal 3.0 x 3.5 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine powers hydraulic pumps (tramming, feed, rotation) and a high-pressure screw compressor. The DTH hammer sits directly behind the bit at the bottom of the hole and strikes it with compressed air while the rotation head turns the string, so penetration does not drop off with depth. The exhaust air flushes the cuttings up the hole. A collar hood and a dust collector with cartridge filters capture the dust, and cuttings from ore holes can be sampled for grade control. Holes are drilled to the design pattern using GNSS navigation, then dipped and logged. A mobile manufacturing unit (MMU) charges them with bulk emulsion or ANFO, primed with boosters and electronic detonators. The holes are stemmed and fired once the area is cleared.
details_to_model: Crawler undercarriage with oscillating track frames; ROPS/FOPS cab with large front window
Boom and feed beam with rotation head, DTH hammer and bit, centraliser, rod carousel (5-7 rods of ~5-6 m)
Dust hood at the hole collar connected by flexible hose to a dry dust collector (cartridge filters) on the rig deck
Compressor and engine compartment with side doors, exhaust stack, fuel tank
GNSS antennas on cab and feed, rotating beacon, work lights
Field model: bench with a drilled pattern (collar markers, cuttings cones), stemming piles, blast exclusion signage and guard posts
hazards_and_safety: Explosives: misfires, flyrock, premature initiation. Comply with DGMS / Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961 and Explosives Rules 2008 in India, or AS 2187.2 in Australia. Blast exclusion zone typically >= 300-500 m for personnel (site-specific)
Never drill into or near old sockets or misfired holes
Silica dust: dry or wet collection, cab filtration
Rig instability near bench crests: set-back from the edge, bunds
sources: AS 2187.2-2006 Explosives - Storage and use - Use of explosives
Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961 (India, DGMS); Explosives Rules 2008 (India, PESO)
Epiroc / Sandvik surface DTH drill rig product literature (class data)
Engineering estimate for patterns and fleet
common_problems: Hole collapse in clay-rich zones: use casing or stemming plugs
Water in holes during monsoon: use emulsion, not ANFO
Fragmentation that is too fine makes sticky fines; fragmentation that is too coarse causes hopper hang-ups. Tune the powder factor

equipment.name: Surface miners (optional selective, blast-free mining fleet)
equipment.function: Cut ore and cap in thin layers without blasting and load trucks directly. Used near villages and forests or where floor selectivity is critical. If adopted as the main ore method, it replaces most drill & blast and part of excavator loading.
equipment.qty_operating: 2-3 (if adopted as primary ore method; 1 for selective floor/sensitive zones otherwise)
equipment.type_selected: Wirtgen 2200SM / 2500SM class surface miner with front-loading conveyor (or windrowing for loader pickup)
equipment.why_this_type: Surface miners are used at East Coast India bauxite and other laterite mines. They give no blast vibration or flyrock, a precise floor (minimising lithomarge dilution and reactive silica), and a sized product (~-100 to -200 mm), which reduces sizer duty.
equipment.alternatives: Drill & blast with backhoe excavators (base case); ripping by large dozers.
key_dimensions: Cutting width ~2.2-4.2 m depending on model; cutting depth up to ~0.35-0.65 m per pass (OEM class, approximate; verify)
Machine length ~11-15 m without discharge conveyor; discharge conveyor slewing, ~8-10 m long, loading height ~4-5 m (OEM class, approximate)
Operating mass ~50-130 t depending on model (OEM class, approximate)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate for UCS ~20-60 MPa bauxite; depends on cutting width and depth

equipment.working_principle: A diesel-driven cutting drum fitted with tungsten-carbide-tipped picks, mounted between the crawler tracks, rotates against the direction of travel. It cuts a layer of set depth from the bench as the machine advances slowly. The cut material is gathered by a primary conveyor and passed to a slewing discharge conveyor that loads a truck travelling alongside, or is laid as a windrow for a loader. Cutting depth is controlled by laser or GNSS levelling, which gives a very flat, accurately positioned floor.
details_to_model: Four crawler tracks on height-adjustable columns, centrally mounted cutting drum with pick holders and picks, drum housing with water sprays
Primary conveyor and slewing/luffing discharge conveyor with loading chute
Elevated operator cab with all-round view, access ladders, handrails
Loading truck travelling alongside; cut bench surface showing parallel lanes
hazards_and_safety: Rotating cutting drum: no access while running, isolation for pick change
Truck-miner interaction during loading: positive communication
Dust: water sprays at the drum
sources: Wirtgen surface miner product literature (class data; verify)

equipment.name: Track-type tractors (dozers) with single-shank ripper
equipment.function: Clearing, topsoil and overburden stripping, ripping soft laterite cap, bench-floor and pit-floor cleanup, dump and backfill shaping, deep contour ripping during rehabilitation, haul-road and ROM-pad maintenance.
equipment.type_selected: ~70-t class crawler dozer (Caterpillar D10 / Komatsu D375A class), semi-U blade, single-shank parallelogram ripper; one unit fitted with a winged-tine rehabilitation ripper
equipment.why_this_type: D10 class gives the ripping force for soft cap and floor preparation while staying mobile between benches and dumps.
equipment.alternatives: D11 class (higher ripping productivity, less mobile); wheel tractor scrapers for topsoil; wheel dozers for pad cleanup.
key_dimensions: Length with blade and ripper ~9-10 m, width over blade ~5.0-5.3 m, height to cab ROPS ~4.0-4.2 m (OEM spec, approximate)
Operating mass ~65-72 t
Semi-U blade ~18-20 m3; ripper maximum penetration ~1.5-2.0 m
equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine drives the tracks through a torque converter and powershift transmission (or electric drive) and a high-sprocket final drive. Hydraulic cylinders control blade lift, tilt and pitch; the operator pushes material in slots to reduce spillage. The rear ripper shank is forced hydraulically into the ground and pulled forward, fracturing laterite or compacted floors so the material can be dozed or loaded. In rehabilitation, winged tines lift and shatter the compacted pit floor along the contour so water infiltrates and roots can penetrate. GNSS machine guidance shows the operator the design surfaces and the ore and topsoil boundaries.
details_to_model: Elevated (high-drive) sprocket, track frames with ~7-8 bottom rollers, grouser shoes ~610-710 mm
Semi-U blade with replaceable cutting edges and end bits, push arms and tilt cylinder
Single-shank ripper with replaceable tip and shank protector, parallelogram linkage, 2 lift cylinders
ROPS/FOPS cab with access ladder and handrails on the left, GNSS antenna masts on the cab roof, rotating beacon, LED work lights
Fire-suppression nozzles in the engine bay, ground-level fuel fill point, radiator guard
Rehabilitation unit: three winged tines at the rear instead of a single shank
hazards_and_safety: Rollover on slopes and bench edges: ROPS, seatbelt interlocks, edge bunds
Interaction with light vehicles: positive communication, proximity detection / collision avoidance
Crushing by ripper or blade during maintenance: lower attachments to the ground, LOTO
Hot engine surfaces and fuel: fire-suppression system
Whole-body vibration and noise
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (Ed. 49/50), D10 track-type tractor data
Koch J.M. (2007) Alcoa's mining and restoration process in south western Australia, Restoration Ecology 15(4 Suppl):S11-S16
operating_tips_and_key_points: Strip topsoil only when its moisture protects the seed bank; keep topsoil and overburden separate.
Rip on the contour during rehabilitation to reduce erosion.

equipment.name: Hydraulic backhoe excavators (primary loading units)
equipment.function: Selective loading of blasted ore (and cap/waste) into haul trucks on 5-8 m benches, following ore/waste and floor boundaries with high-precision GNSS bucket guidance.
equipment.qty_operating: 3 (2 on ore faces of different grade bins, 1 on cap/waste; all three can work ore)
equipment.type_selected: ~200-t class diesel-hydraulic backhoe excavator (Komatsu PC2000 / Liebherr R 9200 / Hitachi EX1900 class), bucket ~10-12.5 m3
equipment.why_this_type: The backhoe digs from the top of the bench down to the floor, which gives selective control at the ore-lithomarge contact and keeps clay dilution and reactive silica low. A dig depth of ~8-9 m matches 5-8 m benches, and the unit loads 90-t trucks in ~5-6 passes. Three faces are kept open for blending. Average duty is ~500 t/h per unit against ~900-1,200 t/h capability; the margin covers selective digging and face moves (engineering estimate).
equipment.alternatives: Face shovel (higher productivity on blasted faces, less selective at the floor); large front-end loaders (mobile, less selective); surface miners (01-SM option).
key_dimensions: Operating mass ~190-210 t; tail swing radius ~5.3-5.6 m; overall width ~5.5-6 m (OEM class, approximate)
Maximum dig depth ~8-9 m; maximum dump height ~7.5-8 m (OEM class, approximate)
Bucket 10-12.5 m3 with 5-6 GET teeth

operating_parameters.unit: t per pass (loose density ~1.4-1.5 t/m3, fill factor 0.9)

equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine drives variable-displacement hydraulic pumps. Control valves send oil to the boom, stick and bucket cylinders, the swing motors and the travel motors. The operator curls the bucket through the blasted muckpile, swings the upper structure through ~60-90 degrees and dumps into the truck body. Bucket-tip GNSS guidance displays the ore polygon boundaries and the design floor, so the operator stops at the lithomarge contact; this matters because the floor clay is high in reactive silica. A payload system weighs each bucket so truck loads are consistent.
details_to_model: Crawler undercarriage with 2 travel motors, ~6-7 bottom rollers per side, triple-grouser shoes ~800 mm
Upper structure: counterweight, engine house with large radiator/cooler, hydraulic tank, fuel tank (~3,000-3,500 L)
Elevated cab with walkways, handrails and a hydraulically lowered access stairway (EMESRT style)
Boom, stick, 2 boom cylinders, 1 stick cylinder, 1 bucket cylinder, hoses routed along the boom
Backhoe bucket with lip shroud, 5-6 teeth and adapters, wing shrouds, wear plates
Central auto-lube, fire suppression, GNSS antennas on the counterweight, LED lights, rotating beacon, rear camera
Model on a bench top loading a truck standing on the same level
hazards_and_safety: Swing-radius crush zone: exclusion barricading; nobody on the ground within reach
Trucks being loaded: driver stays in the cab; never load over the cab
Bench crest and face stability: berms, face-height limits, no undercutting
Hydraulic oil injection and hose bursts: hose shields, depressurise before maintenance
Working at height on the upper deck: handrails, harness points
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (cycle times, fill factors)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Dig the floor last and clean; stay 0.1-0.3 m above the clay contact if grade control requires it.
Present the truck at the best swing angle (~45-70 degrees) and double-side load where possible.

equipment.name: Large wheel loaders
equipment.function: Flexible loading at small faces, rehandle and blending from ROM-pad fingers into the dump hopper, cleanup, stockpile management, excavator cover.
equipment.type_selected: ~95-100 t class wheel loader (Caterpillar 992 class / Komatsu WA900 class), rock bucket ~10-12 m3
equipment.why_this_type: Highly mobile between faces and the ROM pad, and able to blend grade-bin fingers directly into the hopper.
equipment.alternatives: Additional excavator (less mobile); integrated tool carriers for small tasks.
key_dimensions: Length ~15-16 m, width over bucket ~5.5 m, height to cab ~6 m (OEM class, approximate)
Tyres: 50/65R51 for the 992 class (~3.4 m diameter) or 45/65R45 for the WA900/990 class (~3.0 m); model the tyre to the chosen machine (OEM spec sheets, verify)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (992 class rated payload ~20-22 t)

equipment.working_principle: An articulated-frame loader: a diesel engine, torque converter and planetary powershift drive all four wheels, and a Z-bar linkage lifts and crowds the bucket. The machine charges the pile, crowds, reverses and turns to load the truck or hopper. On the ROM pad it takes bucket loads from different grade-bin fingers in a set ratio to make a blended feed.
details_to_model: Articulated frame with centre hinge; large rock bucket with segment edges
Cab with front access stairs, platform handrails, rear-view cameras
Rock tyres (optional tyre chains), mud guards
Payload weighing display, beacon, lights, fire suppression
hazards_and_safety: Articulation pinch point: frame lock during maintenance
Reversing: cameras, radar, proximity detection
Tyre explosion and tyre handling: exclusion zones, nitrogen inflation
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (992 class); Caterpillar 992K and Komatsu WA900 specification sheets (verify tyre sizes)

equipment.name: Rear-dump haul trucks (~90-t class)
equipment.function: Haul ore to the primary sizer dump hopper or the ROM pad, and cap and waste to backfill or dumps.
equipment.qty_operating: 9-10 (~7-8 on ore, ~2 on waste; confirm by haulage simulation)
equipment.type_selected: Mechanical-drive rigid rear-dump truck, ~90-98 t payload (Caterpillar 777 / Komatsu HD785 class)
equipment.why_this_type: Selective mining on several faces with moderate hauls (2-6 km) suits 90-t trucks, which match the 200-t excavators, keep haul-road width and cost moderate, and give fleet granularity. FLEET SIZING (revised): cycle ~27 min (load 3.5, haul 5 km loaded ~12, dump 1.5, return ~8.5, spot/queue 1.5) gives ~200 t/h nominal and ~165 t/h effective. At ~5,000-5,500 operating h/yr each truck moves ~0.85-0.9 Mt/yr. Ore 5.9 Mt/yr needs ~7 trucks; waste ~1.5 Mt/yr on shorter backfill hauls needs ~2. Total 9-10 operating, so 10 operating + 2 spare (engineering estimate).
equipment.alternatives: 136-t (CAT 785 class) trucks (fewer operators, wider roads, less selective); road trains on long public-standard haul roads; trolley-assist or battery-electric trucks for decarbonisation; autonomous haulage.
key_dimensions: Length ~10.5 m, width ~6.1-6.5 m, height (body down) ~5.0-5.2 m, height with body raised ~10 m (OEM class, approximate)
Tyres 27.00R49 (diameter ~2.7 m), so windrow/berm height >= ~1.4 m
Body heaped capacity ~60-65 m3 (liner plates, optional tailgate)

operating_parameters.basis: OEM rimpull curves (approximate); site speed limits apply
Engineering estimate: 2 x 12 h, 7 d/wk roster after availability, utilisation and monsoon losses (corrected from 6,000)

equipment.working_principle: A V-12 diesel drives the rear axle through a torque converter, an automatic planetary powershift transmission, a differential and planetary final drives. Oil-cooled multi-disc brakes and engine/retarder braking control speed on downgrades, which is critical on in-pit ramps and plateau haul roads. At the dump the body is raised by two multi-stage hoist cylinders and the load slides out over the tail. Payload monitoring (from strut pressures) and the FMS log every load (source, destination, tonnage) so ore quality can be reconciled with the refinery.

equipment.working_principle: Two parallel shafts carrying large teeth rotate slowly towards each other. areas.layout_notes: Plateau-top deposit of ~10-20 km2 (life-of-mine reserves for ~30 years at ~5.9 Mt/yr). Mining proceeds in blocks of ~10-50 ha, irregular in plan, 10-30 m deep, on 5-8 m benches with 8% ramps. About 3 faces are active at any time for blending. Haul roads (22-25 m wide) radiate 2-6 km from a central semi-mobile primary sizing station at the plateau edge or centroid of ~5-10 years of reserves; the station is relocated about every 5-10 years. The ROM pad (4-6 ha) sits beside the dump-station ramp. Dump station: ramps rise ~8-10 m to the tipping deck on two sides (MSE walls); the sizer sits below with drives on both sides; MCC/e-house and transformer are ~20-30 m away. The mine infrastructure area (workshop, fuel farm, offices with mine control room, laboratory) is within ~1-3 km of the station on stable ground. The bulk explosives depot and magazines are isolated at their licensed separation distances. Sediment ponds are at low points down-gradient of the pits and pad. Communications towers are on high points. The field conveyor (A02) starts at the sizer and runs to the overland tail.

areas.area_name: Ore transport (mine to refinery overland conveyor system)
areas.purpose: Transport an average of ~5.9 Mt/yr of sized wet bauxite from the mine sizing station to the refinery stockyard over a generic ~20 km route (plateau to valley, assumed net fall ~150 m, i.e. ~0.75% average decline). The system must be reliable, low in operating cost and dust, and have a small land footprint. It is designed for 1,800 t/h so that it can catch up and build pre-monsoon stock.
areas.process_description: SELECTION: overland belt conveyor vs rail for 10-50 km. (a) Conveyor: continuous and electrically driven, so operating cost is low. Labour is low because it is operated remotely from the refinery CCR. It follows terrain with horizontal curves and grades up to ~15-18% (rail ~1-2%). Single loading and discharge points match a single mine and a single refinery. It is proven at this scale: ~50 km overland from the Boddington-area bauxite mine to the Worsley refinery (Wikipedia, 'Worsley Alumina'); ~14.6 km single-flight cable-belt conveyor from Panchpatmali mine to the Damanjodi refinery (verify); Alcoa's Huntly-Pinjarra and Willowdale-Wagerup overlands (lengths to verify); Channar 20 km iron-ore overland (Nordell 1991). (b) Rail: favoured above ~50-100 km, for multiple sources or customers, or where rail already exists. It needs a loop and loadout, a car dumper, rolling stock and crews, and flat gradients (heavy earthworks on plateau escarpments). (c) Slurry pipeline (e.g. Paragominas-Alunorte ~244 km): only for very long distances; requires wet grinding at the mine. DECISION: overland belt conveyor in 2 flights of ~10 km each. The intermediate transfer allows a lower belt rating and splits the risk. It is fed by a relocatable field conveyor (~2-5 km) from the semi-mobile sizer. Sequence: sized ore from 01-CV-001 -> 02-CV-001 field conveyor -> 02-CV-002 overland flight 1 -> intermediate transfer station 02-TS-001 -> 02-CV-003 overland flight 2 -> refinery junction tower -> 03-CV-001. POWER (corrected): the conveyor is NET MOTORING at all normal load cases. Artificial-friction resistance (ISO 5048 / DIN 22101, f ~0.012-0.016, moving mass ~220 kg/m) is ~1.2-1.6 MW per 10 km flight at design load. The gravity credit for a 75 m fall per flight is only ~0.37 MW, so absorbed power is ~0.9-1.4 MW per flight. Regeneration occurs only on local steep descending sections, transiently during stopping, or when only the downhill parts are loaded. Steady-state regeneration would require an average decline above ~2.8% (f x m_moving / m_load ~ 0.014 x 220/111). Active-front-end (AFE) VFDs are still specified for torque control, load sharing and absorbing that local or transient regenerative power. Controlled caliper brakes are required for safe stopping. equipment.working_principle: An endless rubber belt with embedded longitudinal steel cords runs over pulleys at each end and is supported by thousands of idler rolls in between. Drive pulleys at the head and tail transmit torque by friction (Euler-Eytelwein: T1/T2 <= e^(mu*theta)) from motors through gearboxes. A winch take-up keeps enough slack-side tension that the belt does not slip on the pulley or sag excessively between idlers. Over long distances the main resistance is the indentation of the belt's bottom cover as it rolls over the idlers, so a low-rolling-resistance cover compound substantially reduces power. On this route the small average decline only partly offsets the friction, so the drives normally motor. Where a local section descends steeply or only the downhill part of the belt is loaded, the load can drive the belt; the AFE drives then act as generators and the controlled caliper brakes ensure safe stopping. VFDs ramp starts and stops so the stress waves travelling along the elastic belt do not cause slip, belt lift-off in concave curves or excessive tension. Horizontal curves are achieved by tilting (banking) the idlers and holding belt tension within a band so the belt stays centred.

areas.area_name: Bauxite receiving, stockpiling, blending and secondary/tertiary sizing at the refinery
areas.purpose: Receive overland ore at up to 1,800 t/h. Homogenise its quality in chevron blending beds to stabilise the available alumina and reactive silica fed to digestion. Provide strategic storage for mine, overland and monsoon outages. Remove tramp metal, reduce ore to the agreed mill-feed size of -25 mm nominal (P80 ~15-20 mm), sample it for metallurgical accounting, and deliver it to the A04 mill feed bins at ~711 t/h wet average (640 t/h dry). A03 ENDS at the shuttle conveyor 03-CV-005 above the A04 bins. The mill feed bins and weigh feeders (04-BN-001..004 / 04-WF-001..004) belong to A04.
areas.process_description: 1) Ore arrives on 03-CV-001 at the junction tower. An on-line PGNAA analyser and belt scale record tonnage and elemental composition (Al2O3, SiO2, Fe2O3, TiO2) plus microwave moisture, for stacking control. A diverter gate in the junction tower routes ore either to the blending yard or to the emergency stockpile feed conveyor 03-CV-006. 2) A travelling tripper on the yard conveyor feeds a rail-mounted side-boom stacker. The stacker builds two in-line blending beds (A and B) by CHEVRON stacking: it travels the full bed length at constant speed, laying ~300-500 thin layers on top of one another, so each cross-section contains material from the whole build period. 3) While one bed is being built, the other is reclaimed full-face by a bridge-type bucket-wheel reclaimer whose harrow rakes the whole cross-section. This cuts all layers at once and gives a variance reduction (blending effect) of typically ~5-10:1 for chevron beds with this layer count. 4) A strategic/emergency stockpile of ~300-350 kt (~18-20 days) is built by a radial luffing stacker 03-RS-001, with dozer push to extend the pile. Area is reserved for extension to ~45 days at monsoon-climate sites. It is reclaimed by a 992-class wheel loader (988-class backup) into a two-sided ground hopper and belt feeder at >= 750-800 t/h, which covers mill demand when the bridge reclaimer is down. 5) Reclaimed ore passes an overband magnet and a metal detector. 6) Two-stage sizing in the crusher house. There are two parallel lines (1 duty + 1 standby); each line is a secondary twin-shaft sizer (-200 -> -75 mm) feeding a tertiary twin-shaft sizer (-75 -> -25 mm nominal, P80 ~15-20 mm), as agreed with A04 for single-stage ball milling. 7) The mill-feed conveyor 03-CV-004 carries crushed ore to the A04 bin building. The mechanical cross-belt sampler 03-SA-001 on 03-CV-004 takes the metallurgical-accounting sample of refinery feed (ISO 8685); the cutter aperture is practical here because top size is -25 mm. 8) A reversible shuttle conveyor 03-CV-005 at the A04 bin-top elevation distributes ore to the 4 mill feed bins (04-BN-001..004) by bin-level priority. Lime and spent liquor are added in A04. 9) Dust control: water sprays and fog at transfers, fog cannons on the stockpiles, and a pulse-jet baghouse on the crusher house and transfer points. Stockyard runoff drains to a lined settlement pond and is recycled. A mobile-fleet wash bay serves the loaders and dozers. No caustic is handled in A03; first caustic contact is in A04 grinding.

areas.layout_notes: Stockyard at grade on the refinery's upwind side (relative to prevailing wind towards the offices), adjacent to the grinding area (A04). The junction tower (with analyser, scale and diverter) is where the overland enters. From it, an in-line yard ~500-550 m long x ~110-130 m wide runs: incoming conveyor and stacker rails on one side, two beds (each ~50 m wide, ~200-220 m overall) end to end, bridge reclaimer rails straddling the beds (~52-55 m span), and the reclaim conveyor on the opposite side. The optional roof shed (03-RF-001, ~60-65 m span, ~28-32 m high) covers the beds. The emergency stockpile (~300-350 kt; ~250 x 120 m footprint, 15-18 m high, with reserved extension area) lies beside the yard, fed by 03-CV-006 and radial stacker 03-RS-001, with its two-sided ground hopper discharging to 03-CV-002. An inclined covered gallery (~12-15 degrees) rises from the yard to the top of the crusher house (~40-45 m high, two lines of secondary over tertiary sizers). The mill-feed gallery 03-CV-004 (with the sample station) rises to the A04 bin building, where shuttle 03-CV-005 runs at the A04 bin-top elevation (~+25 m) over the four A04 bins. A ~6 m perimeter road surrounds the yard for maintenance, fire access and loader cleanup. Electrical substation and MCC rooms are near the crusher house; the wash bay is at the yard access road; the settlement pond is at the yard's low corner.
interfaces: A02: receives up to 1,800 t/h from 02-CV-003

A04 Grinding: A03 ends at shuttle 03-CV-005 discharging into A04 mill feed bins 04-BN-001..004 (A04 owns bins and weigh feeders 04-WF-001..004); crushed product -25 mm nominal, P80 ~15-20 mm, ~711 t/h wet average, bin filling up to 1,100 t/h; shuttle elevation set by A04 (~+25 m)
Laboratory/QA: accounting samples from 03-SA-001 (after sizing), PGNAA data, reconciliation of refinery feed with mine (A01) FMS tonnages
Utilities: process/raw water for dust suppression, compressed air for the baghouse, power

decisions.reason: Recalculated as ~20-45 ha/yr for 10-20 m ore (~140-350 kt/ha), with topsoil ~20,000-135,000 m3/yr. 60-110 ha/yr is kept only as the Darling Range comparison. Rehabilitation is rewritten for deep pits (partial backfill, lowered plateau landform, benched planted walls).

decisions.finding: Dilution counted twice: ROM 6.2-6.4 Mt vs refinery consumption ~5.9-6.0 Mt (mining_logistics)
decisions.reason: ROM mined and delivered = refinery feed +- stock change = ~5.9 Mt/yr wet. Ore loss and dilution are treated as an in-situ-to-ROM adjustment that lowers the delivered grade, which the bauxite factor already reflects. There is no reject stream.

decisions.finding: A02 'regenerative on downhill sections' misleading; conveyor is net motoring (mining_logistics)
decisions.reason: Checked with ISO 5048: friction ~1.2-1.6 MW per flight against a ~0.37 MW gravity credit gives ~0.9-1.4 MW absorbed. The regenerated-power stream is replaced by a power-demand stream. AFE VFDs and controlled brakes are kept for local and transient regeneration, and the dynamic-analysis load cases are named. Installed power is adjusted to 3 x ~750-1,000 kW and the belt class to ST1600-ST2500, take-up force to ~60-150 kN.

decisions.finding: A03/A04 interface inconsistent: crush size, bin count/size, shuttle elevation (mining_logistics)

A -25 mm product cannot be made reliably in one sizer stage from -200 mm (ratio ~8 vs ~3-5 per stage), so a tertiary sizing stage is added: 2 lines x 100%, each secondary (-75 mm) over tertiary (-25 mm). The live capacity of each bin is left to A04: the reviews differ (700-1,000 t vs 600-900 t).

decisions.topic: A01 deposit model used by the 3-D models and lessons (post SME model review)
decisions.decision: Generic plateau deposit: ferricrete caprock 0.5-3 m over friable gibbsitic ore (4-15 m) on kaolinitic clay. Caprock is drilled with 89-127 mm top-hammer/DTH rigs on a ~3.0 x 3.5 m pattern; ore is free-dug/ripped by backhoe in 1-2 flitches. Caprock is classified by grade-control assay: ore to the sizer where available Al2O3 and reactive SiO2 meet cut-off, otherwise backfill (~50 % assumed ore, to be confirmed).
decisions.alternative: East Coast India-type hard massive bauxite (DTH 115-165 mm on 5-8 m benches, or surface miners) - see open questions.
decisions.basis: Aligned with the A01 multi-agent SME model reviews (2026-11)

open_questions: Live web verification was again blocked (WebSearch HTTP 403). WebFetch worked only for Wikipedia: 'Worsley Alumina' confirmed ~50 km overland from the Boddington mine; the NALCO, Damanjodi and Alcoa pages gave no conveyor or mine-method detail. These remain unverified: NALCO cable belt (~14.6 km, ~1,800 t/h), Alcoa Huntly-Pinjarra / Willowdale-Wagerup overland lengths, East Coast drill & blast / surface miner practice, Wirtgen and OEM class data, and loader tyre sizes.

Tertiary sizing to -25 mm on wet, sticky gibbsitic ore at ~1,000 t/h per line needs vendor testwork (MMD or equivalent). If it is not proven, the fallback is -40 mm feed with A04 re-running the Bond calculation at F80 ~20-25 mm (~10-20% more mill power), or hammer/impact crushers.
A04 to confirm the live capacity per mill feed bin (reviews range 600-1,000 t) and the bin-top/shuttle elevation (~+25 m assumed) so the A03 gallery 03-CV-004 can be fixed.
Caprock and laterite cap: treated as waste or blended low-grade ore depending on assays. Confirm the reactive silica and available alumina limits for cap blending with the refinery process team.

Climate basis: confirm whether the generic site is monsoonal (India East Coast). If so, decide (a) the base-case blending-yard roof 03-RF-001, (b) the emergency stockpile at ~20 days vs 30-45 days, and (c) whether pre-monsoon stock is held at the mine ROM pad or at the refinery.

Surface miners vs drill & blast as the main ore method. This depends on proximity to communities and forest, blast-vibration limits, ore UCS and pick-wear trials. Base case is drill & blast; surface miners are an option.

Site terrain for the generic overland route: assumed ~20 km with ~150 m net fall (~0.75% average). Local steep descending sections must be defined for brake and AFE sizing; a net-uphill route would increase installed power.
Truck class: 90-t class selected for selectivity on 5-8 m benches. The owner may prefer 136-t class (fewer trucks, wider roads) or electrified/autonomous haulage; confirm before modelling.
Primary sizing station relocation interval (~5-10 years assumed) and whether a fully mobile in-pit sizer is preferred.
Use of the PGNAA on-line analyser (radioactive-source licensing) vs laboratory-only quality control is an owner preference. If kept, include it in the plant radiation-source register.
Grade-control specification limits (reactive SiO2 ceiling, available Al2O3 floor, blending variance targets) to be set jointly with the refinery process team.

Outside A01-A03 but affecting the shared layout and bulk handling: refinery-to-port mode (8 km conveyor in A16/A17 vs 30-60 km rail in A20), and whether a coal-fired steam basis needs coal import, unloading and a stockyard. One decision is needed before 3-D site modelling.
